script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

MARY, 50s, sits on the couch, surrounded by papers. Her face shows the weight of responsibility. Her son JIM, 20s, enters the room.

JIM
(cheerfully)
Mom! You look overwhelmed. What's going on?

MARY
(sighs)
Just bills, work projects, and the house needs repairs. I feel like I'm drowning.

JIM
(smiling)
Well, I'm here to help. What can I do?

MARY
(gratefully)
Thank you. I need to paint the living room and fix the leaking roof.

JIM
I'll help you with the painting. But the roof, I'll need to call a professional for that.

MARY
(smiling)
You're a lifesaver.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

Mary and Jim start painting the living room walls, chatting and laughing.

JIM
(pausing)
You know, I've been thinking about moving out and getting my own place.

MARY
(surprised)
Really? Why?

JIM
I feel like I'm holding you back. With your work and all these house repairs.

MARY
(reassuringly)
You're not holding me back. This is our home, and I want you here. Besides, I can't imagine living without your help.

JIM
(smiling)
I feel the same way.

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

They sit at the kitchen table, eating dinner together.

MARY
You know, when I was your age, I always dreamed of traveling the world.

JIM
(surprised)
Really? Why didn't you?

MARY
I met your father, and we started our family. But I've always regretted not fulfilling that dream.

JIM
Well, it's not too late. Why don't we travel together?

MARY
(smiling)
That's a great idea.

INT. MARY'S STUDIO - NIGHT

Mary works on her latest painting, inspired by their conversation. Jim enters the room.

JIM
(admiringly)
Wow, this is beautiful. Where did you find the inspiration?

MARY
(smiling)
You did.

INT. LIVING ROOM - MORNING

They pack their bags, ready to embark on their journey.

JIM
(excitedly)
We're finally doing it, Mom!

MARY
(gratefully)
Yes, we are. Together.

INT. AIRPORT - DAY

They board the plane, waving goodbye to their old life, ready for new adventures.

FADE OUT.

THE END
